counterfactuals.reason: The failure occurred because termination depended on manual developer intervention via a single workstation that was retired, eliminating the carrier for the termination function. The proposed change implements cloud-native termination signals (batch job completion webhooks calling cloud API or cloud-side lifecycle policies based on idle duration) that execute entirely within the cloud environment. These mechanisms do not depend on local workstation state, developer awareness, specific tooling on particular hardware, or manual intervention. The termination function would execute automatically either upon batch job completion (via webhook) or when idle duration thresholds are exceeded (via lifecycle policy), completely bypassing the failed carrier (retired workstation) and removing the dependency that caused this specific failure.

The failure occurred because (1) cleanup trigger was lost when stateful workstation disappeared and (2) no monitoring existed to detect orphaned resources. The proposed change provides two alternative mechanisms that would each independently prevent this failure: automated alerts would detect machines active beyond job completion window, notifying operators of the 40 idle machines within the alert timeframe rather than after two weeks; OR persisted credentials in multiple accessible locations would enable cleanup execution from alternative systems when the original workstation was retired. Either branch of the OR would break the causal chain that led to undetected idle machines accumulating charges.
